source.note: The registry's own approved boundary document. Not redrawn, not approximated, not sourced from any third party.

registry_metadata_snapshot.states_provinces: Matabeleland North, Midlands, Mashonaland West, Mashonaland Central

artifact_facts.crs: OGC:CRS84 / EPSG:4326 (WGS84 longitude, latitude) — the KML default; no reprojection performed

transformations_applied.detail: Every KML coordinate carried a third value of exactly 0. The GeoJSON is 2D.

All five KML rings are clockwise; RFC 7946 exterior rings are counter-clockwise, and Earth Engine interprets winding on geodesic polygons. The point set of every ring is unchanged and the reversal is verified by round-trip comparison against the KML.

transformations_deliberately_not_applied: No coordinate rounding, simplification or densification.
No repair of the part 1 / part 5 overlap described below.
No dissolve or union of the five parts.
No inward buffer — that is an analysis-time operation per ADR-011 and docs/data/conventions.md.

geometry_validity.method: pure-python ring closure, pairwise segment intersection, range checks

part_overlap.method: latitude-band integration of x-interval overlap; converged: 2,000 bands 0.29249 km2, 8,000 bands 0.28839, 32,000 bands 0.28862
part_overlap.other_pairs: all nine remaining pairs have zero intersection
part_overlap.detail: Parts 1 and 5 are the Binga and Nyaminyami parcels, which the project description states share a border (PD p17). 29 vertices of part 1 fall inside part 5 and 12 of part 5 inside part 1, with no shared vertices - a digitising sliver along that common border, not a duplicated polygon.
part_overlap.consequence: Area must be computed on the union. Left exactly as delivered by the registry.

boundary_area.what_it_is: The total area of the four Rural District Council parcels the project is drawn over - what this geometry delineates.
boundary_area.source: PROJ_DESC_902_16AUG2013.pdf p98 (document id 110200000335895): “stakeholder consultations have been elaborated for the entire boundaries of the RDCs of 1’077’930 ha”. Repeated verbatim in AFOLU_PROJ_ELEM_902_01July2014.pdf and in the 2012 project description.
boundary_area.our_method: geodesic union on the WGS84 ellipsoid: sum of parts 1,072,667 ha less the 0.2886 km2 part 1/5 intersection
boundary_area.agreement: -0.49% against the documented figure. The file's own embedded Area attributes sum to 1,077,930.24 ha, matching the project description to 0.24 ha (2e-5%), which identifies this geometry as the dataset the PD describes.

vcs_project_area.what_it_is: The FORESTED portion - woodland plus open woodland at project start - inside those boundaries. This is the VCS accounting area. It is not a polygon in this file.
vcs_project_area.source: PROJ_DESC_902_16AUG2013.pdf p4 “The project area of 784’987 hectares of forest (consisting of woodland and open woodland)”; p7 Table 1 “Total project area (ha) split into regions, WL an OPW” summing Binga 157,652 + Hurungwe 131,480 + Mbire 269,513 + NyamiNyami 226,341 = 784,987; p44 Table 12 labels the same parts “forest 2011 only”; p98 “The VCS project area (forested area) is about 784’987 ha”.
independently_confirmed_by: VALID_REP_902_19AUG2013.pdf (Aster Global validation report): Binga 157,652.50, Nyaminyami 226,341.46, Hurungwe 131,480.28, Mbire 269,513.10, “Total Project area = approximately 784,987 ha”
025-VCS+CCB Kariba_VerReport_final-03January2020.pdf: “784,987 hectares of Woodland (WL) and Open Woodland (OWL) in four Rural District Councils”
220908_CCB_VCS_Kariba_REDD_MR5_v4_clean.pdf (2022 monitoring report): same sentence, same figure
vcs_project_area.consistency_check: 1 - 784,987 / 1,077,930 = 27.2%, the exact figure the PD itself quotes for the share of additional land consulted. Implied per-parcel forest shares are Binga 74.7%, Hurungwe 87.6%, Mbire 77.7%, Nyaminyami 61.2% - all plausible for Zambezi-valley miombo.

registry_area_field.what_it_is: UNEXPLAINED. The 'Acres/Hectares' field on the Verra registry project page.
searched_for_it_in: VCS_CCB Verra Quality Control Review Report_902, 30JUN2026 (18 pages)
registry_area_field.result: No figure between 735,000 and 765,000 hectares appears in any of them. Every document that states a project area states 784,987 ha. The registry field is not traceable to the project record and is treated as registry metadata of unknown provenance, not as a measurement.
registry_area_field.action: Recorded, not reconciled, not used. Nothing in the geometry or the case was adjusted to match it.

area_cross_check.verdict: The geometry is the RDC boundary dataset the project description names, and it agrees with the documented figure to 0.5%. The earlier 43% discrepancy was a comparison between a boundary area and a forest area - two different quantities, not two estimates of one.

notes: ADR-011 builds the treated unit as registry_boundary INTERSECT mask MINUS exclusions, inward-buffered 300 m. This artifact is the registry_boundary term: the RDC parcels, not the forest inside them.
That is the right input. ADR-011's baseline-forest mask (Hansen treecover2000 >= 30%) does the forest extraction itself, from a source independent of the project's own classification.

It follows that the eligible area ADR-011 computes is directly comparable to the project's own 784,987 ha forest claim, from independent data. That comparison is a validation opportunity, not a rule: nothing in ADR-011 changes, and the eligible area is whatever the pinned inputs produce.
The inward buffer is applied after masking, per ADR-011, so it is not baked into this artifact.
The part 1 / part 5 overlap (0.2886 km2) must be dissolved before any area or zonal computation, or the sliver is counted twice.

The five parts correspond to the five parcels the project documents name - Binga, Nyaminyami, Hurungwe and Mbire in two pieces. Whether the GAUL 2015 level-2 units of those names contain them is unverified here and belongs to #23.

not_verified_here: Whether the geometry lies entirely within Zimbabwe (needs an administrative boundary dataset; #23).
The origin of the registry's 747,801 ha field - absent from every project document searched. Only Verra can explain it.

Per-polygon identification against a named RDC. Bounding boxes and forest-share arithmetic are consistent with Binga, Hurungwe, Mbire (two parts) and Nyaminyami, but the KML's placemarks are unnamed and carry no authoritative label.
